extracted.intended_audience: early-career assistant professors (tenure-track) and institutional research/limited-submission administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for institutions and eligible early-career faculty about the Searle Scholars Program: a limited-submission grant mechanism that funds independent research of recently appointed assistant professors on the tenure track. Covers who and what the award supports and that institutions — not individuals — receive the grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited submission mechanism / institutional nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program is a limited submission award program that makes grants to selected academic and research institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the program is limited submission, institutions must follow internal selection/nomination processes to identify candidates (see the program's 'Process & Eligibility' page for full procedures). The grant is awarded to institutions rather than directly to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target: support for independent research
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are intended to support the independent research of outstanding early-career scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award funds the research program of the identified scientist; applicants/institutions should emphasize the candidate's independent research plan and potential. See 'Award Information' for allowable uses and funding details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — early-career assistant professors on tenure track
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible candidates are outstanding early-career scientists who have recently been appointed as assistant professors on a tenure-track appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'recently been appointed' implies a defined post-appointment time window (not specified on this page); applicants and institutions should consult the detailed eligibility rules on the program website to confirm timing, prior appointments, and other qualifying conditions.
